promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Geometry/layout authority and edit target

Use case: sketch-to-render, game tile sheet. Image 1 is the authoritative geometry guide and edit target. Reskin it into finished painted game art, preserving every shape, band, hole, beam and position, the exact 1536x1024 canvas and all empty white space. Do not move, rescale, rotate, merge or add pieces. Everything is a building's ROOF seen from directly overhead. The sheet holds five separate pieces. PIECE 1, THE FIELD (x 0-767, y 128-895): ONE continuous seamless stretch of roof, two by two cells of 384 px with no gaps, borders or frames. Keep the guide's grain (courses, ribs, seams, plates) exactly where it is and evenly spaced, so the left edge continues into the right edge and the top into the bottom when tiled. Even, quiet weathering, no single large feature near an edge. PIECE 2, THE EAVE EDGE (x 800-1503, y 40-103): the roof's finished outer edge as a long straight strip, its outside at the top: the lit lip along the top, the edge band, a shaded foot along the bottom. Identical all along. PIECE 3, HOLED (x 800-1151, y 136-487): one cell of the same roof punched through by a shell: the near-black middle is an OPEN HOLE onto the dark room below; paint its ragged rim of broken, bent and splintered roofing, cracks and grit, scorching round the rim. PIECE 4, COLLAPSED (x 1168-1519, y 136-487): one cell where the roof has fallen in: the strip along the top is the roof still standing with a torn lower edge, below it a slab of roof sagging and tilted down, and broken joists hanging; the near-black is OPEN onto the dark room below. PIECE 5, BURNT THROUGH (x 800-1151, y 520-871): one cell burnt through by fire: charred, cracked rafters and a broken purlin over the open dark room, with a few blackened scraps of roofing left on them, ash, faint ember glow in the cracks. Keep every near-black void a flat, plain near-black. Material: the dorsal plating of a crashed Domain-era Explorarium survey mothership, now a roof over its interior: broad stepped armour slabs of different sizes in pale teal-green and sage with khaki and bone segments, exactly where the guide puts their seams; the seams fine and low in contrast, never a regular grid; kitbashed greebles, pipework and tarnished brass only in the one narrow machinery channel; rust-brown grime in the seams, mottled weathering, crash dust and scorch, a vent block and a hatch, no hazard stripes in the field; the edge the hull's heavy armour rim, buckled and scorched; holes punched craters in the plate with bent petals and torn structure; the burnt state blackened hull frames. Painted like Starsector's own derelict ship sprites. Straight 90-degree overhead orthographic camera, top-down like a strategy-game map tile, no perspective. Sun from the upper left. Hand-painted gritty science-fiction game-tile look like Starsector, restrained palette, coarse readable detail that survives being shrunk to about 32 to 64 pixels per cell. No text, letters, numbers, labels, watermark, UI, people, plants or extra objects; no border; white everywhere outside the five pieces. Change only material, surface detail and subtle shading, never placement, size or silhouette.
